checkpoints.name: Project Setup
checkpoints.built: Set up the Express server, the /public + /data folders, package.json, README and .gitignore. The server boots and serves a hello-world route plus a static landing page.
checkpoints.hard: Getting the gitignore right so node_modules and the future .env never get committed.
checkpoints.change: Sketch the URL map on paper before writing any routes.
checkpoints.aiUsage: AI helped scaffold package.json scripts; I wrote the routes by hand.
checkpoints.ab: Tried both nodemon and node --watch in dev — kept nodemon because the brief required it.

checkpoints.name: Register and Login
checkpoints.built: Built /api/auth/register, /login, /logout, /me. Sessions are signed with express-session and users persist in data/users.json.
checkpoints.hard: Realizing that I had to validate username characters server-side, not just in the form.
checkpoints.change: Hash passwords with bcrypt next time — the brief says plaintext for learning, not for life.
checkpoints.aiUsage: AI suggested express-session config; I tightened cookie sameSite/httpOnly myself.
checkpoints.ab: Compared a single combined endpoint vs separate /login and /register — split them for clearer error messages.

checkpoints.name: Game Board UI
checkpoints.built: Added a 3x3 CSS-grid board with click handlers and a turn indicator pill at the top of the card.
checkpoints.hard: Keeping the cells perfectly square at every screen width without media-query gymnastics.
checkpoints.change: Move the board state into a tiny class instead of a few module-level variables.
checkpoints.aiUsage: AI proposed an aspect-ratio trick for the grid; I picked 1:1 and tested at 320px wide.
checkpoints.ab: Tried both SVG lines and CSS borders for the win highlight — kept the colored cell background since it's simpler.

checkpoints.name: Human vs Human
checkpoints.built: Implemented full PvP same-screen play with proper turn switching, win detection across all 8 lines, and draw detection.
checkpoints.hard: Off-by-one bugs in the win lines array — I had to write them out twice to be sure.
checkpoints.change: Add unit tests for checkWinner before moving on.
checkpoints.aiUsage: AI generated the LINES table; I verified each entry by hand.
checkpoints.ab: Tried both eight separate ifs and the LINES array — array won for readability.

checkpoints.name: Save Games
checkpoints.built: Finished games append to data/games.json with mode, board, result, opponent, and a timestamp. Added a recent-games panel on the play page.
checkpoints.hard: Concurrent writes corrupted the JSON once — fixed by writing to a tmp file and renaming.
checkpoints.change: Lock the file or batch writes if there are ever real concurrent users.
checkpoints.aiUsage: AI suggested the tmp+rename trick after I described the corruption symptom.
checkpoints.ab: Considered a single games.json vs one file per user — kept one file because the brief says so.

checkpoints.name: Groq AI Wired Up
checkpoints.built: Added the groq-sdk client behind GROQ_API_KEY, a PvP/PvAI toggle, and a server route that returns a legal AI move with an in-character comment.
checkpoints.hard: The model sometimes returned non-JSON or invalid moves on its own. I made the server compute the move locally and ask Groq only for the comment.
checkpoints.change: Add a small retry with stricter system prompt before falling back.
checkpoints.aiUsage: AI helped draft the prompt; I rewrote it once I saw it returning prose instead of JSON.
checkpoints.ab: A: ask Groq for {move, comment}. B: compute move locally + ask Groq for {comment}. B was reliable, kept it.

checkpoints.name: Difficulty and Personality
checkpoints.built: Easy plays random, medium mixes random and minimax, hard runs full minimax. Personalities are trash-talker, cheerleader, and zen master, applied to the Groq comment.
checkpoints.hard: Minimax was easy; making medium feel imperfect-but-threatening took several tries.
checkpoints.change: Expose a slider so I can tune the medium random-vs-optimal ratio without redeploying.
checkpoints.aiUsage: AI scaffolded the minimax shape; I added the score adjustment so it prefers faster wins.
checkpoints.ab: Tried 30/70, 50/50, and 70/30 random-vs-optimal for medium — 50/50 felt most fun.

checkpoints.name: Leaderboard and AI Stats
checkpoints.built: Built /api/stats/leaderboard ranking by points (3/1/0) then win rate, and /api/stats/ai with breakdowns by difficulty and personality.
checkpoints.hard: Result is stored from the player's perspective, so AI win rate is 'losses' from the player side — wrote that comment into the route.
checkpoints.change: Add a server-side filter by date range so I can see weekly stats.
checkpoints.aiUsage: AI suggested the points formula; I picked the tiebreakers.
checkpoints.ab: Compared sorting by raw wins vs points — points is fairer to people who play a lot of draws.

checkpoints.name: Profile and Extended Profile
checkpoints.built: Added a full profile page with 9 data fields: username, display name, bio, favorite personality, favorite difficulty, country, games goal, avatar color, and join date. Users can view and edit their profile. The /api/users/profile route handles GET and PUT. Also added id and role fields to every user record.
checkpoints.hard: Deciding which profile fields are editable vs read-only — kept username and joined date as read-only.
checkpoints.change: Add profile photo upload so the avatar isn't just an initials circle.
checkpoints.aiUsage: AI helped me think through what fields connect meaningfully to the game (favPersonality, favDifficulty).
checkpoints.ab: Considered putting edit inline vs a separate edit mode — separate mode was cleaner on mobile.

checkpoints.name: Admin Dashboard
checkpoints.built: Built /admin page and /api/admin/* routes behind a role === 'admin' middleware. Admin can see overall stats (users, games, games today), manage all users, and create/edit/delete announcements. Regular users are blocked with a 403.
checkpoints.hard: Making the redirect happen cleanly on the frontend when a non-admin visits /admin — checking the role from /api/auth/me before rendering.
checkpoints.change: Add an audit log so I can see what the admin changed and when.
checkpoints.aiUsage: AI suggested the middleware pattern for checking role server-side before any route handler runs.
checkpoints.ab: Considered a separate admin subdomain vs a /admin route — kept it as a route since the whole app is one server.

checkpoints.name: Announcements and Game History
checkpoints.built: Active announcements from announcements.json now appear on the home page — admin edits are instantly visible to all users. Also built the Game History page with result/mode/difficulty filters and a board replay modal that shows each game's final state and move order.
checkpoints.hard: The board replay needed to re-run win-line detection on the stored board array — pulled the same LINES constant used in the game engine.
checkpoints.change: Add pagination on history for players with 100+ games.
checkpoints.aiUsage: AI helped write the filter + map pipeline for the history table.
checkpoints.ab: Tried showing the move list as a timeline vs a badge row — badges are more compact and still readable.

checkpoints.name: Home Page and Navigation Polish
checkpoints.built: Replaced the empty index.html with a real home page: hero section, feature cards, live quick stats, and announcement feed. Updated the nav to include History, Profile, and Admin links dynamically based on login state and role.
checkpoints.hard: The nav had to stay simple on mobile — used flex-wrap so links wrap gracefully instead of overflowing.
checkpoints.change: Add a hamburger menu for very small screens.
checkpoints.aiUsage: AI suggested fetching leaderboard data to power the quick stats on the home page.
checkpoints.ab: Tried showing a random Tic Tac Toe board on the hero vs a text description — kept text since the board needed JS to animate.

checkpoints.name: Final Polish and Data Seeding
checkpoints.built: Added 5 seed users with full extended profiles, 5 seed games with userId cross-references, and 5 seed announcements. Verified all 8 pages load and all JSON requirements (5+ records, 4+ fields, id field, cross-file references) are met. Fixed styles for the modal overlay, progress bar, and admin announcement row layout.
checkpoints.hard: Making sure every page works for both logged-in and guest users — some routes needed soft redirects instead of hard 401s.
checkpoints.change: Add end-to-end tests to verify each page loads and the key API routes return correct data.
checkpoints.aiUsage: AI helped seed realistic game data and cross-checked the requirement list.
checkpoints.ab: Considered lazy-loading each page's JS vs one shared bundle — kept per-page ES module scripts since the app is small.
